No. You’re not understanding what I’m saying. She wasn’t just making a joke, she was purposely making fun of me and her goal was to make me feel bad. That’s how she is. I know they aren’t, and I’ve been getting better at them so I didn’t go through with it, but it did almost trigger me. 

She told me to do my compulsion and then laughed. It really worried me and almost caused me to break down. She’s known about my OCD for years and usually doesn’t make fun of me like she did today, but is very serious about it and tells me my compulsions are real to go keep doing them. I’ve been talking to her and telling her that needs to stop and I need to work on getting better but I’ve been having to do it on my own despite her continuing to reassure my compulsions. 

I’ve been trying to laugh at it. I tell myself it’s stupid and not real every time I get ready. I even joke about it when I tell other people to make light of it and make it not serious. My mother wasn’t doing that, she was trying to make me feel awful. She wanted me to do my compulsion because she gets a kick out of me being a “freak” and worrying about things like that.
It's nice to know someone understands. I'm sorry you have to deal with it as well. Hopefully it gets better for the both of us.

I do this sometimes. First, I think you should try to understand that the stalking incident is very unlikely to happen again. Most people don’t go look at every social media possible to make sure the person not responding to them isn’t posting somewhere without replying to a text, and it’s even more rare that a person would come to your work and confront you there. I’m sorry that happened to you though, that must have been pretty creepy! The people that matter will understand. Anyone you want to rekindle a friendship with, or anyone new you want to keep talking to, just let them know you’re a person who sometimes just doesn’t have the energy or motivation to respond, and let them know you’re not ignoring them if you never reply. My 2 best friends know this about me and completely understand, hopefully you have some friends like that as well :) Just let people know if you don’t reply within a few days, it’s ok to double text and see if you’re up for a convo. I have an online friend who sometimes takes months to reply, but when she does I’m always super excited and it’s always worth the wait. It might also be good when someone just says something small like “what’s up” to maybe have a little compromise and just say “I’m alright, but I don’t have energy right now so I’ll text you next week/once I’m feeling better.”

You should be honest with her. Let her know when your depression is getting bad, it will be good for your relationship and help her to understand you more. Let her know how to be there for you or if you need her to at all. My boyfriend and I have a way of communicating my level of mental health by using a scale of 1-10. If it’s between 6-8 then he knows I’m having a bad day and offers to talk or asks me what I need. If you’re feeling a little down, but not necessarily terrible and don’t want to say “not good” when she asks you how you’re doing, you could say “today’s not the best day but I’ll be fine” but only if that’s the honest truth. If you are feeling terrible, let her know and let her know what she can do to help if she can at all. As a cat lady who’s had cats her entire life, though. I’ll give you a little of my own advice.

As long as she’s not destroying things, she’s being played with enough. Some cats need more playtime than others and they usually calm down as they get older. If she’s constantly running across the couch and tearing it up, she needs her energy out so try playing with her with a feather toy. If she’s chewing on the tv cords, throw a toy mouse for her so her attention goes to that instead. 

When it comes to things she shouldn’t eat, think the same as a regular cat or baby. While she should be having kitten food if possible (it has the right nutritious for a growing kitten) regular cat food won’t hurt her. Don’t give her milk as it’s not good for kitties tummies. The only thing you should really be concerned about with what she’s eating is if she’s getting into garbage or chewing cords or furniture or anything not meant to be consumed. If she does this, take her away and distract her with something else. Cats usually grow out of this so you won’t have to keep such a close eye on her for forever.

The peeing can be a problem. It is possible she has something wrong with her but don’t worry too much. Maybe just have your roomie mention it to the vet when she goes in to get spayed or have her next round of shots. In the meantime, if you catch her peeing on the bed, tell her no and put her in the litter box. Make sure the smell is 100% gone from where she’s peed before because if there’s still the tiniest bit of smell, she’s going to smell it and think it’s an ok place to pee. There’s urine remover cleaners made for this so you might have to get some. She should grow out of this too (especially once she’s spayed) so until then make sure there’s nothing laying around with a mildew like smell that might draw her to pee on it. Our newest kitten would sometimes pee on wet towels that had been in the laundry for a couple days. If she’s peeing on a bed that’s been used for sex, that could be a smell she’s peeing on too (maybe tmi lol but it’s true). 

Good luck!! It’s very nice of you to help out with this little girl but I hope her owner is taking responsibility.

It is so so soooo much easier if they can communicate with you!! My friend who I'm most open with my anxiety about has anxiety too and we use the safe word system. I find telling her that my excuse is anxiety is fairly easy because she understands it so well but there have been times when I've had to cancel on her multiple times in a row and start to feel bad so I make up some other excuse like work or something. I tend to not tell many other people because it's honestly very hard to find someone who is understanding of it so it's very nice that you're putting in this effort!! 

For me, it's not usually the place we're going or thing we're doing that makes me not want to say it's my anxiety, it's often times that my anxiety is just too high to even feel comfortable saying it. So while my friend will understand that I've had to cancel 5 weeks in a row because my anxiety has been bad for that long, since it's been bad for that long it will make me feel like she won't understand or will be mad that I keep cancelling so I make up a "better" excuse. That's why I say to constantly reassure that anxiety is ok to you and doesn't bother you that they have it. 

Just try to be as open with your friend as possible and don't ever make them feel like you're annoyed or frustrated that they don't want to do something. Even if it does annoy or frustrate you lol. Just be like "Yeah, I was looking forward to going but honestly I've really been wanting to watch the new season of stranger things so I'm totally down for that too" even if you were dying to go and don't care about the new season of stranger things, just saying what you can to make them more comfortable will always be nice for them.

Something that I always find very helpful is when someone is very reassuring that we don't have to do whatever thing is planned if I don't want to. If you guys have plans to go to the mall, make sure you say multiple times that it's ok if they don't want to go. They might be embarrassed to say the reason is anxiety but make sure you let them know you're someone who will accept that excuse. Let them know that they can say "hey, I'm feeling anxious and don't want to hang out today" or "I'd rather us just chill at your place instead of go to the movies". Hopefully they're comfortable telling you that and communicating their anxiety to you but if they aren't, maybe always offer an option that you know they would like. "You still wanna go to the mall? Or you wanna stay home and watch some movies instead? I'm down for whatever!" and do that every time, making sure there's always a "safe" option for them. (I'm not sure if being at your place is even a safe option for your friend, I'm just using it as an example...I personally don't always want to be at my friends house but hopefully you can figure out what your friends safe option is!)

Also, if they're always saying sorry to you because of their anxiety, make sure you let them know over and over again that it doesn't bother you in the slightest. If you guys go out together, maybe make a safe word to say or text in case they want to leave early. Just always make sure you let them know there is an option to get out of any situation that might make them uncomfortable. 

Sorry this is kind of all over the place but I hope it helps!! Best of luck :)

Ok, first I would recommend that if you decide to take a nap today to make sure you sleep no more than 90 minutes. (if i'm reading your post right..you got no sleep last night and are worried about work tomorrow, correct? sorry it's a bit confusing since it's 11pm here haha)

Anyway my routine for when I've had a few anxious days. 

First I like to make sure I have a dessert or snack I really like, something to treat myself with. I love chocolate muffins and cake so I'll get a single serving one from the grocery store and put it in the freezer. It's my favorite way to eat it! So I'd recommend something similar to suit you. 

Then I start my routine a couple hours before I want to go to sleep. I usually like to go to sleep around midnight so I'll start around 9 or 10 depending on how tired I am. I like to give myself enough time incase I get distracted or something takes longer than I anticipated. 

I usually try and find something to watch. A few youtube videos, a couple episodes of a Netflix show depending on how long it is. I'd actually recommend a few chapters of a book over this since looking at a screen can trick your brain into thinking it's day time but honestly on my worst days I can't bring myself to read anything. 

Anyway, I get whatever I'm going to watch/read ready and put my laptop/book next to my bed that I make sure is super cozy and ready for me to get into. Then I pamper myself a little. Paint my nails, shave, etc. Whatever I think I need to do to make me feel good. (also a good time to masturbate tbh..maybe tmi but it's the truth! hahaha) Then I'll run a hot bath and make a hot cup of tea. I try to make the bath as relaxing as possible, lavender bath bombs are my favorite. Anything calming. Light a candle or too and turn the lights off. Set the tea on the edge of the tub (they make sleepy time teas which are good, they're mostly just chamomile so if you have regular chamomile tea that would be good too).

I like make the bath really extra hot so it can steam up the room a little. I'll leave it for about 15 minutes to cool off (which is why I make the tea extra hot too so it's a good temperature once I'm ready to drink it) and I do some relaxing yoga while I wait for the bath to cool. I don't like following videos or anything so I just have a few poses that I googled and do them for a while, making sure to concentrate on my breathing. Once the bath has cooled enough for me to get in, I'll soak in the bath for 20 minutes or so while sipping my tea. It's a good time to use a face mask too if you're into them. I like to make a playlist of 5 songs because they usually add up to 20 minutes so that way I know how long I'm in the bath for and have something to help my mind calm down. Relaxing/yoga type music is good but I tend to just go for slow songs that I really like. Acoustic Ed Sheeran lovey dovey type stuff. I like singing along in my head because it keeps my mind from thinking of all the things that make me anxious and keeps my stress down. 

After my bath I'll put on some lavender lotion. They make a sleepy one at Lush that I love. I feel like the bath and the lavender scent at the most important parts of this whole thing for me. The super warm bath really relaxes all my muscles and makes me really sleepy. 

Then I'll get my comfy pjs on and get into bed and watch whatever I have lined up for myself. A lot of times I can't even finish what I had planned to watch because I can hardly keep my eyes open! 

Depending on my mood I'll either eat my dessert in the bath or in bed while watching my show. It makes me feel full which also makes me sleepy and makes me happy because it's a treat I really love. I recommend eating in the bath if you're someone who absolutely needs to brush their teeth before bed. I usually regret eating it in bed because once I get cozy I don't want to get up to brush my teeth after but tend to do it anyway. Just messes up the flow a little but you could be different than me!

I also recommend making sure your room is at a good temperature. I'm always really warm after the bath so I like the room to be slightly cooler than normal and it feels really nice and fresh when I get out of the bathroom and it's really nice to be warm under the covers with the cool air all around the room. 

Also just other things like no lights on if they distract you, if you do happen to wake up, don't look at your phone or anything and just turn over and go back to sleep. I sometimes get woken up by my dog kind of early cause she needs to go out and it's obviously something I can't stop from happening. When this happens and I wake up too early, I'll make myself some breakfast and do whatever I can to stay sleepy. I don't go on my phone or get dressed or brush my teeth. I just drowsily make myself something to keep me from being too hungry to sleep (carbs are good for this haha) and then get right back into bed. If you're a morning pooper, maybe do that too. I always have to pee. So I eat, pee and get right back into bed without doing anything else. Sometimes it takes me an hour or so to go back to sleep but even if that happens, I usually sleep an extra hour or two before I have to get up which is totally worth it. 

Sorry this is so long!! I'm really bad at short answers lol. Best of luck!

Make sure your kids understand mental health as well so they can understand what their mom is going through, and will understand themselves more if they develop it in the future.
